Round I · while coding
Implementation assumptions
Where the ticket was ambiguous: the reading the coder chose.
  1. assumption55% confident A failure hides the grid instead of keeping stale rows
    Read the other way: Keep the last rows visible under the error banner
    Why 55%: The spec says a failure must not look like a result, and stale rows under a new query would. Showing the previous rows greyed out is a reasonable UX that the spec does not exclude.
    

    2. 

  2. assumption60% confident Type-mismatch 400 applies to every REST endpoint, not only the list
    Read the other way: Scope the 400 to listOwners and keep 500 elsewhere
    Why 60%: The spec needs page=abc to return 400, and a 500 for malformed input is wrong everywhere. Still, /api/owners/abc changing from 500 to 400 is a contract change nobody asked for.
    

    3. 

  3. assumption60% confident Allowed sizes and the sort default stated in OpenAPI descriptions
    Read the other way: A custom OpenAPI customizer emitting an integer enum and default
    Why 60%: springdoc renders allowableValues as strings, which Spectral rejects, and drops a default that contains a comma. Prose keeps the lint green, but machines cannot read the 5/10/20 rule from the schema.
    

    4. 

  4. assumption65% confident An empty page within a non-empty result shows a "go back" row
    Read the other way: Jump to the last valid page automatically
    Why 65%: The spec only forbids claiming "no matches" and requires navigation to stay available. Auto-jumping would send an extra request nobody triggered.
    

    5. 

  5. assumption70% confident "Unrepresentable" page means its offset overflows Hibernate's int
    Read the other way: Accept any int page and let a huge offset fail at query time
    Why 70%: The spec (specs/owner-list/spec.md:23↗) demands a 400 for unrepresentable pages without defining the term. Capping at MAX_INT/20 is the tightest bound that holds at every allowed size, but a lower business cap would be equally defensible.
    

    6. 

  6. assumption75% confident Invalid parameters rejected by bean validation plus a @OneOf constraint
    Read the other way: A custom exception that rest throws and rest.error maps
    Why 75%: packages.puml forbids rest → rest.error, so a custom exception would need an architecture change. Spring's own HandlerMethodValidationException keeps both packages independent; the cost is one small constraint annotation.

Issue #25: Add pagination to Owners grid
victorrenteaopened on May 13, 2026
  • The grid should be sortable by any column
  • The grid should be paginated in pages of 5, 10, or 20 rows per page
Requirements of the OpenSpec change paginate-sort-owners
  1. Owner list page contract — GET /api/owners SHALL return HTTP 200 with exactly content and totalElements as its page-envelope fields. content SHALL contain existing owner DTOs with their pets, pet types, and visits; totalElements SHALL count all matching owners before pagination.
  2. Paging inputs and bounds — The API SHALL use zero-based page with default 0 and size with default 10. Valid page sizes SHALL be only 5, 10, and 20. Negative, non-integer, or unrepresentable page numbers and invalid sizes SHALL return HTTP 400 rather than being silently normalized.
  3. Business-key sorting — The API SHALL accept only sort=name,asc, name,desc, city,asc, or city,desc, defaulting to name,asc when omitted. Name SHALL order by last name, first name, and owner ID; City SHALL order by city, last name, first name, and owner ID. The selected direction SHALL apply to every field in the chain.
  4. Preserved last-name filtering — The API SHALL preserve case-sensitive literal last-name prefix filtering. An omitted or empty lastName SHALL match all owners. Pagination and sorting SHALL operate on the filtered set, with totalElements reflecting that set.
  5. Bounded list data access — Owner listing SHALL retrieve owner rows only for the requested page and associations only for selected owners. A full non-empty page SHALL require at most three SQL SELECT statements, including counting, association loading, and response mapping, independent of the number of matching owners or pets.
  6. Owners grid navigation — The grid SHALL display a page of owners, offer page sizes 5/10/20, indicate the current range and total, and expose sorting controls only for Name and City. The initial grid state SHALL correspond to API defaults. Existing Bootstrap styling, owner-detail navigation, and Add Owner behavior SHALL remain available.
  7. Grid state transitions — A submitted search, page-size change, or sort change SHALL reset the page index to 0. Search SHALL preserve the active sort. Page and sort navigation SHALL use the submitted filter, not unsubmitted input edits. Page state SHALL remain local to the screen rather than being added to the URL.
  8. Latest request wins — Only the latest list request SHALL update the displayed rows, total, loading state, or error state. Leaving the screen SHALL cancel any outstanding list subscription.
  9. Empty results and failures are distinct — After a successful response with totalElements=0, the grid SHALL show a no-owners message containing the submitted prefix and hide the paginator. Request failures SHALL display an explicit error rather than being presented as successful empty search results.
  10. Unchanged authorization and owner operations — Existing owner-list authorization and all owner-detail, count, create, update, delete, nested pet/visit, and chatbot owner-detail/MCP contracts SHALL remain unchanged. All in-repository list consumers SHALL use the new page envelope.
